title: Envisioning the Applications and Implications of Generative AI for News Media
venue: CHI ’23 Workshop on Generative AI and HCI
extended_summary:
This workshop paper examines how generative AI could be used in newsroom workflows and what ethical, professional, and design challenges such use would create. The authors focus on two broad stages of news work—newsgathering and news production—and ask which tasks might benefit from generative support, how such tools could affect journalistic agency and creativity, and which journalistic values should shape system design.

Rather than reporting an intervention study, the paper is a conceptual synthesis grounded in prior literature and industry reporting. It discusses possible applications of large language models such as summarizing complex documents, querying unstructured text, brainstorming story angles, assisting with collaborative writing and revision, and generating social media content. Throughout, the authors emphasize that these uses should be human-supervised and embedded in interfaces that support transparency, explanation, and user control.

The paper is situated in the context of professional journalism and newsrooms, especially drawing on examples from U.S. media organizations and an Associated Press report on AI readiness in American newsrooms. No student, school, or classroom population is studied. There is no experiment, no educational intervention, and no quantitative analysis of motivation, writing outcomes, or ChatGPT effects.

The main conclusion is that generative AI may be useful for augmenting newsroom tasks, but only if designed through value-sensitive, human-centered processes that account for risks such as hallucination, privacy leakage, over-reliance, bias, costs, and threats to journalistic autonomy. For the verification question raised here, this paper is clearly not the alleged 2026 randomized trial, contains no 25-plus-25 secondary student writing experiment, and should be excluded from any quantitative synthesis on ChatGPT-based writing feedback in high school because it is not an education study and provides no eligible outcome data.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a workshop position/concept paper about generative AI in journalism, not an empirical education study. It reports no student sample, no intervention implementation in schools, no randomization, and no original outcome statistics on motivation or writing.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper provides no causal or quantitative evidence on educational outcomes, so no impact estimate can be derived. It is irrelevant to quantitative synthesis on ChatGPT-based writing feedback in high school.
